newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Focus - Pakhoed set for growth after 1996 transition.
newsitem.headline: Focus - Pakhoed set for growth after 1996 transition.

text.p: Dutch distribution and logistics group Pakhoed NV on Tuesday reported a 12 percent rise in 1996 net profit from ordinary operations and said the fruits of restructuring would be double-digit growth this year.
Net profit from ordinary operations in 1996 was 138.3 million guilders, up from 123.6 million in 1995, and at the high end of market expectations.
In a weaker Amsterdam Exchange, Pakhoed shares rose 2.10 guilders to 61.40 guilders.
However, restructuring charges, which were mainly taken in the first half of the year, sliced the 1996 total net profit to 75.5 million guilders, well below 1995's 121.5 million.

The one-off charges were taken for the reorganisation of Pakhoed's Rotterdam-based units and for the sale of troubled subsidiary Furness, which combined port activities, car dealerships and logistics.

Pakhoed said 1996 was very much a transition year that had seen its full acquisition of chemicals distribution firm Univar as well as the divestment of Furness and the Rotterdam restructuring, but its performance had noticeably picked up in the second half of the year.
The changes would result in a burgeoning bottom line this year.
"We expect to see a significantly higher result (from ordinary operations) than this year.... That means double-digit growth," Pakhoed chairman Klaas Westdijk told a news conference.
Behind the growth would be improvements at Univar and the turnaround of Pakhoed's Rotterdam-based activities.
This year, Univar in North America intends to increase its gross margin by a half percent point.
"This may not sound that much, but it is equivalent to 65 million guilders," said Westdijk.

In oil storage, Pakhoed's activities in Rotterdam, which were loss-making in 1996, are expected to return to profits this year. Restructuring remains the key, but the market itself has already shown signs of improvement.
"The market has noticeably improved from January 1. A contango market emerged in the first two months of this year and we have done reasonably well," executive board member Gerard Krans said.
A stronger dollar will also help the company.
"For every 10 guilder cent rise of the dollar, our profit rises by 4.5 million guilders," Westdijk said.

The dollar's impact is even more pronounced as Pakhoed drifts away from its Dutch core. In 1996, 20 percent of Pakhoed's turnover came from the Netherlands. This year, the percentage will fall below 10 percent, Westdijk said.
Analysts reacted very positively to last year's figures and the positive outlook.
"The results are great and it is set for growth. Pakhoed is delivering without any tricks," said Gert Jochems of NIB Securities.
"It was somewhat better than the market expected and similar for the 1997 outlook... We maintain our buy (recommendation) and there is room for upgrading," said BZW's Andre Mulder.
